title: Federal Reserve Board announces it has made the joint findings with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency required for the OCC to approve a request by Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A., for an exemption under section 23A of the Federal Reserve Act
summary: The Federal Reserve Board announced on March 26, 2026, that it has made the joint findings with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) required for the OCC to approve Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A.'s request for an exemption under section 23A of the Federal Reserve Act. The exemption request was submitted to enable an internal corporate reorganization involving the bank's affiliate, Morgan Stanley Europe SE, headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, Germany. Section 23A establishes statutory limits and requirements governing transactions between a bank and its affiliates.
key_points: The Federal Reserve made joint findings with the OCC to approve Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A.'s section 23A exemption request
The exemption was sought to facilitate an internal corporate reorganization
The reorganization involves Morgan Stanley Bank's affiliate, Morgan Stanley Europe SE in Frankfurt, Germany
Section 23A of the Federal Reserve Act establishes limits and requirements on bank transactions with affiliates
The announcement includes links to statements by Vice Chair Philip N. Jefferson, Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle W. Bowman, and Governors Michael S. Barr and Lisa D. Cook
This is a bank-specific regulatory action with no broader monetary policy implications
why_it_matters: This is a routine bank regulatory matter approving a section 23A exemption for Morgan Stanley's internal corporate restructuring. It does not affect monetary policy, interest rates, or market structure. It is relevant only to parties with direct exposure to Morgan Stanley Bank or its European affiliate.
